newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Escorts, Yamaha JV plans upgrade.
newsitem.headline: India's Escorts, Yamaha JV plans upgrade.

text.p: Escorts Yamaha Motor Ltd, a joint venture between India's Escorts and Japan's Yamaha Motor Co., said on Thursday it planned to invest 5.25 billion rupees to upgrade existing motorcycle manufacturing facilities as well as set up a new plant near New Delhi.

Escorts chairman Anil Nanda said the two companies, now equal partners in the joint venture, plan to expand the equity base to 500 million rupees through a public issue of shares in mid-1997. Each would hold 26 percent after the share issue.
The new plant costing 1.5 billion rupees would make scooters, which the Escorts group would be making for the first time, company officials said.
"Mr Nanda disclosed that the equity base of Escorts Yamaha Motor Co Ltd will be expanded to over 500 million rupees," the joint venture said in a statement.

Later, Nanda told a news conference that total equity, currently at 100 million rupees, would go up to 520 million rupees. Of this, Escorts and Yamaha would together account for 270 million rupees, he said.
The shares would be issued at a premium yet to be decided by merchant bankers, Nanda said.
